title: My Pineapple Tallow Balm Routine: A Weird Thing That Works
body:
Okay so I was just sitting here after washing my face and I realized I’ve been doing this for like three weeks straight now. The routine. It’s not even a routine, it’s just this thing I do. I’m on my couch, it’s probably 9:30, and I just finished wiping off that sunscreen that always feels like it leaves a film. My face was tight. You know that feeling. And I just reached for the little jar without even thinking. That’s the weird part. I didn’t have to think. My hands were just dry from all the hand-washing earlier—I was cleaning the coffee maker and it was gross—and my face felt like a desert. So I grabbed it. The pineapple tallow balm. The whipped one from that Etsy shop. It’s become the thing I do now. My tallow balm routine, I guess. I didn’t plan it. It just happened.

## How This Beef Tallow Thing Even Started

Look. Putting beef fat on your face sounds insane. I know. I thought it was a joke. My friend sent me a link and I was like, are you for real? It’s called a whipped tallow balm. Made from grass-fed beef suet, whipped up into this cream. From France, apparently. I pictured like, bacon grease in a tub. But she swore by it. Said it fixed her winter hands. And my skin last month was… not good. Flaky. Red patches near my nose. That rough texture on my forehead. I’d tried that fancy lotion in the blue bottle. Fifty bucks. Did nothing. So I was like, fine. Whatever. It was spring but my skin didn’t get the memo. Still acting like it was February. I ordered the pineapple scent because it said “tropical escape” and I needed one. Badly. It arrived in a little box. Jar was smaller than I thought. I opened it. Smelled like… pineapple? But not candy pineapple. Like if a pineapple was subtle. Or maybe just fruity. I don’t know how to describe it. Cheerful. I put a tiny bit on the back of my hand. It was cold. Solid but soft. I rubbed it in. It was gone. Like, it just vanished into my skin. No grease. No shine. Just… my hand was softer. Weird. So I tried it on my face that night. Half expecting to wake up a pizza. I didn’t.

## My Actual Daily Skincare with Tallow

So here’s what I actually do. It’s not complicated. I’m not a skincare person. I have like, three products.

At night is the main event. After I wash my face—just with that basic gel cleanser, the cheap one—I pat it dry. Not all the way. A little damp. Then I scoop out a bit of the balm. Amount? Like, half a pea? A small pea. I warm it between my fingers. It melts super fast. Then I just press it all over. Forehead, cheeks, chin, neck. Sometimes I rub it in a little. Sometimes I just pat. It feels… I don’t know. It doesn’t feel like anything after a minute. It just sinks in. My skin doesn’t feel tight anymore. It feels… normal. Like it’s not freaking out. That’s the best way I can put it. I’ll put a thicker layer on any super dry spots. My elbows have been a disaster since forever. I put some on them too. Then I just go to bed. No sticky pillow. That was a big fear. Nothing.

Morning is faster. If I’m not wearing makeup, I’ll sometimes just splash water on my face and press a tiny, tiny bit of the tallow balm on my cheeks before sunscreen. Just the driest parts. It makes the sunscreen go on smoother. Doesn’t pill. If I’m having a really dry day, I’ll mix a tiny dab with my foundation. Sounds crazy. Works though. Makes it less cakey.

And my hands. God, my hands. I wash them constantly. They crack. I keep the jar by the kitchen sink. After I do dishes, I dry my hands and put a little on. It soaks in before I can even touch the fridge handle. No greasy marks. That alone is worth it. How to use tallow balm? Just… use it. Wherever you’re dry. It’s not science.

## The Weird Part Where I Got Distracted By The Smell

So I was using it the other night and my cat jumped up on the bed. He sniffed my face. Seriously. He like, leaned in and did that slow blink. And it hit me—the smell. It’s not strong. It’s not a perfume. It’s just this… vibe. The pineapple tallow balm scent. It’s not a piña colada. It’s not fake. It’s like the idea of a pineapple. A sunny, vacation feeling. But quiet. It doesn’t linger. It’s just there for a second when you open the jar, and then it’s on your skin, and then it’s gone. But it makes the whole process feel… nice. Like a tiny treat. I was putting it on and I remembered being at a hotel pool as a kid. The plastic lounge chairs. That smell of sunscreen and chlorine and… something fruity from the bar. This balm smells like the good part of that memory. Not the chlorine part. Anyway. The point is, it makes a boring skincare step feel a little less boring. Which is maybe why I keep doing it.

## What Actually Happened to My Skin

I wasn’t expecting miracles. Honestly.

But after a week, the flakiness around my nose was just gone. Not better. Gone. The tight feeling after washing my face? Gone. My hands… they look like hands again. Not sandpaper. The skin on my arms is smoother. I was putting it on my elbows for a few nights and now they’re not all rough and ashy. It’s wild.

The best thing is how it absorbs. They say tallow mimics human skin sebum. Soaks in deep. I believe it. It doesn’t sit on top. It just becomes part of your skin. I’ve used oils before. They just slide around. This isn’t like that. It’s like my skin just drinks it and says thank you. I’m on my second jar now. I got one for my mom too. She has that winter damage on her knuckles all year round. She texted me last week “what is this magic butter.” So yeah. It just works. I don’t have a better explanation. My skin is calm. It’s hydrated. It doesn’t look “glowy” in that Instagram way. It just looks… healthy. Normal. Like it’s not mad at me anymore.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. From what I read, it’s really similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. So it absorbs like it belongs there. It doesn’t just coat the surface. My face seems to think it’s good. No breakouts. Just happy skin.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not for me. And I can get clogged pores. This stuff sinks in so completely there’s nothing left to clog anything. It’s not like a heavy oil or Vaseline. It’s more like a super nutrient-dense moisturizer that disappears.

**What does the pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
It’s fruity but not sweet. Not a candy smell. It’s bright. Like a hint of tropical fruit without being overpowering. It smells like summer vacation feels. But subtle. The smell fades pretty fast after you put it on.

So that’s it. That’s my tallow balm routine. No ten-step process. Just a little jar of whipped beef fat that somehow fixed my dry skin. If your skin’s being difficult, and the fancy stuff isn’t cutting it, might be worth a shot. I got mine from a small shop on Etsy. I’ll probably order another one soon. My elbows haven’t been this smooth since… I don’t know when. Anyway. It just works.
